history_desc: Sree Seetha Lakshmana Hanumath Sametha Ramachandra Swamy Temple, Inagalore — 180 Years of Sacred Heritage, Communal Harmony, and Devotional Journey.
village_harmony_badge: 🕊️ Inagalore Grama Panchayath • Communal Harmony & Unity (~230 Houses • ~1200 Population)
village_harmony_desc: Inagalore is a small Revenue Village and Grama Panchayath having around 230 houses with approximately 1200 population comprising of all religions, castes, sects and sub sects. All the villagers live with mutual love, affection, and high respect towards other religions, celebrating festivals of all faiths with shared happiness and devotion.
history_section_pooja_title: Chronology of Nithya Pooja Kainkaryams (1845 to Present)
history_tree_desc: The sacred Peepal Tree (Aswartha Vrukshamu / Ravi Chettu), which was around 300 years old, began growing in multiple directions and encroaching in 360 degrees, causing cracks to the temple structure. Following extensive discussions and expert advice from Temple Sculpture Experts, Veda Pandits, Builders, and Villagers, Santhi Homas were performed and the tree was safely removed in May 2024. With generous support from Inagalore villagers, Pancharathnam and Nuligommu families, and devotees, the temple was completely renovated in 2024.
history_punah_desc: Punah Pratishtha was completed in October 2024 with the original Krishnasila idols of Sri Rama, Seetha, and Lakshmana along with New Bhaktha Anjaneya and Dhwaja Stambha. An 11-member Trust was formed under the name 'SRI SEETHA LAKSHMANA HANUMATH SAMETHA RAMACHANDRA SWAMY TEMPLE TRUST' (Reg No: 8/2025, PAN: ABKTS6306C).
festivals_desc: As the Temple does not have fixed income sources, Nithya Dhoopa Deepa Naivedyam (Daily Pooja), Saturday Abhishekam, and Annual Festivals are sustained through the generous contributions of devotees and villagers.
pending_works_title: Pending Works & Appeal for Devotee Support
pending_works_desc: Inagalore village is located in Sri Sathya Sai District, Andhra Pradesh, which has the second lowest rainfall in India after Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. All farmers are dependent on rain-fed crops with very meagre income. Having already donated beyond their means, the Trust appeals to generous donors to help complete the following sacred pending works.

timeline_1845_desc: Late Sri Subbaramappa Pancharathnam established the sacred temple with Blackstone deities in Inagalore.
timeline_1800_desc: Sri Pancharathnam Subbaramappa Gaaru established the sacred temple with community elders.
timeline_1900_desc: The temple flourished as a hub of Vedic recitations, Ramayana discourses, sathakams, and literary service.
timeline_2020_desc: Initial blueprints drawn blending ancient Shilpa Shastra stone craftsmanship with enduring structural excellence.
timeline_2024_desc: Inauguration of the majestic granite temple complex built with 100% community devotion and shramadaana.
